tagline.text: A rainforest botanic garden on the slopes of Mount Makiling, inside the UPLB campus

location.label: Location
location.text: College of Forestry area, UPLB, Los Baños, Laguna, at the foot of Mount Makiling

children.text: This botanic garden of about 300 hectares sits at the foot of Mount Makiling inside the University of the Philippines Los Baños (UPLB) campus. You can stroll among rainforest trees, palms and bamboo, and it makes an easy day trip from Manila.

Makiling Botanic Gardens is located in the College of Forestry area of the University of the Philippines Los Baños (UPLB) in Los Baños, Laguna. The park covers about 300 hectares at the foot of Mount Makiling and lies within the Mount Makiling Forest Reserve (about 4,244 hectares). It was established in 1963 under Republic Act No. 3523 to support forestry and plant science instruction and research, as well as tourism, education and public recreation. The forest reserve was declared an ASEAN Heritage Park in 2013.

This is not a flashy destination like a beach or a theme park. Instead, it is a place to walk quietly in the shade of huge rainforest trees, listen to the creek, and rest over a packed lunch with the kids. Inside the garden, native, endemic and exotic plants are planted in separate sections. The best-known ones are the Philippinensis Row, the Dipterocarp Arboretum, the palm and bamboo collections, and the National Corner, which gathers the national symbols sampaguita and anahaw.

Molawin Creek runs through the middle of the garden, and a stairway leads down to the water. Higher up, a dipterocarp forest and a palm plantation continue, and because the road is steep, many visitors ride a jeepney up from the entrance. The garden is managed by the university as an "outdoor laboratory," so you often see forestry students practicing plant taxonomy. First-time visitors should check the signs and map at the entrance and plan their route. The garden is large and the upper part is a continuous climb, so it is easier to walk the lower, flatter sections first and go uphill only if you still have energy. Reading the name tag on each tree takes longer than you expect, so set aside at least
2–3 hours

It is close to Manila, so one day is enough. You can combine it with other Laguna sights such as Pagsanjan Falls or Lake Pandin, and pairing it with the hot spring town of Los Baños on the same Mount Makiling area fills a day nicely. Opening hours and fees can change depending on the university's circumstances, so check the latest announcements on the official Makiling Botanic Gardens page (makiling.center) or its social media before you go.

One section has native Philippine trees planted in rows, and the arboretum collects dipterocarps, the signature trees of Southeast Asian tropical forests. Looking up at the thick trunks of tall trees such as bagtikan gives you a real sense of the scale of a rainforest. Trees carry name tags, which is especially nice for plant lovers.

You can compare many species of palms and bamboo in one place. The shape of the stems and the size of the leaves differ from species to species, which makes for good photos. Passing through the bamboo groves, you can hear the wind and it feels cool even at midday.

This corner gathers plants that represent the country, such as the national flower sampaguita and the national symbol plant anahaw. It offers a short introduction to Philippine nature and culture, and it is a handy spot to explain things when you visit with children.

blocks.title: Molawin Creek and the Stairway Trail

children.text: A stairway leads down to Molawin Creek, which flows through the inner part of the garden. Standing by the water, the air feels cool even at midday. The steps and rocks can be slippery with moss, so please go down slowly.

Mount Makiling is said to have recorded about 120 bird species, about 50 mammal species, 19 reptile species and 6 amphibian species (citing a 2013 study). In the garden, too, you can see butterflies and birds in the early morning or afternoon, and with luck you may spot hornbills.

There is a rest area under the trees with a pavilion, fountains and picnic tables. It is common to see families and student groups spreading out packed lunches here. There are not many places to eat inside the area, so it is best to bring snacks and water.

Trained UPLB student guides lead guided tours of the garden. You hear about plant names, the role of the forest and conservation, so you get more out of it than walking alone. Group visits and field trips require advance booking, so please inquire beforehand. News about the garden is available through official announcements and social media posts.

Start with the National Corner and Philippinensis Row. It is not yet hot, so walking is comfortable and it is a good time to see birds and butterflies.
Walk slowly through the Dipterocarp Arboretum and the palm and bamboo sections. Reading the name tags as you go,

Have a meal around the UPLB campus or in Los Baños town, then head to the hot spring area to end the day.

items.title: Full-Day Course
items.subtitle: Botanic garden and Los Baños hot springs

children.text: Leave Manila. On weekday mornings SLEX gets congested, so it is better to set out early.
Arrive at the garden and either sign up for a guided tour or walk on your own. The guided tour costs
(2025 press figure; it may vary by group size and duration, so confirm on site).
Have lunch in Los Baños town. There are many inexpensive restaurants for students around UPLB.
Head to the hot spring and mud spring area on the same Mount Makiling and relax. See the
Mount Makiling & Los Baños
entry for details.
Take a ride back to Manila before sunset. Roads can be congested on Friday and Sunday evenings.

Take a bus bound for Laguna from Manila (around Buendia, Cubao or Taft) to Los Baños. According to a 2014 blog, companies such as BLTB, Green Star and JAM ran toward Santa Cruz. Check the current operators and fares at the terminal.

Get off at the Los Baños crossing (around Los Baños Junction) and transfer to a jeepney bound for the UPLB College of Forestry. Tell the driver to drop you at the "botanic garden" or "College of Forestry." Travel guides agree that buses from Cubao or Buendia run to Los Baños and Santa Cruz, but confirm the exact boarding point and fare on site.
From Manila to Los Baños takes roughly
2–3 hours
depending on traffic.

items.title: By Car, Taxi or Grab from Manila

children.text: Take the South Luzon Expressway (SLEX), exit at Calamba, then follow the national highway to Lopez Avenue in Los Baños town. Continue along the road toward UPLB and you will find the Makiling Botanic Gardens sign.
Vehicles cannot enter some parts of the garden, so you use the parking space near the entrance (based on a 2014 visit report; follow the instructions on site).
For a group, hiring a vehicle for the day is convenient. Fares require negotiation and checking locally.
Between Los Baños town and UPLB you travel by jeepney and tricycle. Because the road up into the garden is steep, many visitors take a jeepney.
If you arrive by air, land at Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL) and continue by the bus or vehicle described above.
The garden is open all year, but with many mountain paths and stairs it is slippery and muddy on rainy days. Walking is much easier in the dry season,
November–May
. To avoid the midday heat, it is best to arrive right after opening at
In the rainy season, afternoon showers are frequent and leeches increase. Check the weather and official announcements before you visit.

There is no accommodation inside the garden and not much to eat either. Cheap restaurants and cafes popular with students cluster in Los Baños town and around UPLB, so it is easiest to eat there. Another option is to bring snacks and water and eat them in the garden's rest area.

If you want to stay overnight, use a hotel or guesthouse in Los Baños town or a hot spring resort in the same Mount Makiling area. On weekends and holidays it is better to book early. Prices vary by season, so check booking sites and locally.

Because it is on a university campus, there are many students and researchers at mealtimes. After visiting the garden, it is a good experience to go to the area around the UPLB main gate or Los Baños town and try Filipino home cooking or student canteen dishes. Los Baños is also known for buko pie (coconut pie) and its hot spring town, so drop by to fit your schedule. Opening hours differ by shop, so check locally.
The most pleasant time is the dry season, November to May, around 8 a.m. right after opening.
Wear non-slip sneakers or trekking shoes rather than sandals. Stairs and dirt paths are slippery when wet.
Bring long pants and insect repellent against mosquitoes and leeches.
Prepare plenty of water and snacks. It is better not to expect a store inside the garden.
If you have a student ID, bring it, since you may get the ₱45 student rate.
Guided tours and group or field-trip visits need advance inquiry. Phone +63 49 536 2637, official information at makiling.center.
Do not pull up or break plants and trees, and take your trash with you. Forest conservation is a point the guides here emphasize.
Hours and fees can change, so check the latest announcements before you visit.
Bring a camera and a power bank. Photos tend to come out dark in the shade of trees, so daytime hours are best.
The Mount Makiling Forest Reserve is managed by the university. Mountain hiking trails beyond the botanic garden may be closed or require a permit, so be sure to check the latest announcements.
On rainy days the stairs and rocks by the creek are very slippery. Hold the handrail when going down.
Watch for falling branches when passing under trees, especially on windy days.
There are leeches and mosquitoes in the forest reserve. Prepare with long clothes and repellent.
Children slip easily on dirt paths and stairs, so keep an eye on them.
It gets crowded when many groups visit, so weekday mornings are best if you want a quiet walk.
